name: RHIC Interaction Point 6 (STAR experimental hall)
notes: STAR has operated continuously at this interaction point since RHIC's first collisions in 2000 through RHIC's final run on 2026-02-06 (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026).

Secondary sources (search-engine summaries of physics papers, not checked against the papers) describe this as RHIC's 6 o'clock interaction point. That clock-position label is not recorded as a sourced fact because no primary or official source consulted states it.

summary.plain: The experimental hall on the RHIC particle-collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory where the STAR detector records the debris of particle collisions.
summary.technical: One of the two interaction-region halls that remained active on the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory, housing the STAR detector from RHIC's first collisions (2000) through its final run (2026). The recorded point is the centroid of the hall's building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 100 m precision), not a geodetic survey point.
